hints: The counting position advances by k each time, wrapping around the remaining circle.
A Fenwick tree can mark which labels are still present and select the label by its live rank.
Use zero-based ranks carefully: after removing one person, the next starting index is the removed rank modulo the new size.
analogy: Count around a shrinking circle by rank, using an indexed list of the people still present.
example: For n=7,k=2, the first removed is 2; continue counting from the next person among the six remaining.
algorithm: Maintain live labels in a Fenwick tree. For remaining size m, compute the next zero-based removal rank, select rank+1 among live labels, remove it, and update the rank modulo m.
correctness: The rank update is the circular counting rule, and the order-statistic structure returns exactly the label currently occupying that rank.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
